preconditions.description: Attacker must be the contract owner

violation_target.exploit_hint: As the contract owner, call the setMaxWalletAmount function with a parameter that will cause maxWalletAmount to be set to zero. Since maxWalletAmount = _tTotal / _maxWalletAmountPct, passing a very large _maxWalletAmountPct (greater than _tTotal) will result in integer division yielding zero. This will effectively prevent any non-excluded wallet from holding any tokens, potentially causing a denial-of-service for regular users.

attempts.vulnerability_analysis: The vulnerability is owner privilege abuse where the owner can set maxWalletAmount to 0 by calling setMaxWalletAmount with a very large divisor. The oracle verification checks if maxWalletAmount == 0, which we can achieve by exploiting the owner's setMaxWalletAmount function with type(uint256).max as the parameter.
attempts.attack_strategy: Impersonate the contract owner and call setMaxWalletAmount with type(uint256).max to set maxWalletAmount to 0 through integer division truncation.
attempts.step_by_step_plan: 1. Get the owner address from the contract. 2. Start prank as the owner. 3. Call setMaxWalletAmount(type(uint256).max). 4. Stop prank. 5. Verify maxWalletAmount == 0.
